items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] The protection of public health requires similar guidance and oversight. AI can strengthen biosurveillance by finding signals across disparate data, model and predict outbreaks, and help allocate scarce resources. We must build governance into our health system’s infrastructure that includes testing standards and protocols, continuous monitoring, ethics oversight, user education, and clear lines of accountability. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.summary:
Leaders have to use the technology themselves: experiment, push the boundaries and learn what works. When people see that AI matters to you, it sets the tone and encourages others to engage with it.

We did not mandate usage targets. Instead, we made the technology relevant. Our business transformation team demonstrated workflows tailored to different functions, while videos, showcases, challenges and an early AI bounty surfaced ideas from across the firm. [...] The real value we’ve seen from AI so far hasn’t been about reducing cost or needing fewer people, but freeing our people to focus on the more human side of their work, meeting with clients, coaching their teams and mentoring the future leaders of our industry.

> _“It’s been about…freeing them up to then do the more human side of their work.”_

—Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer, Gilbert + Tobin [...] My team is now able to use it to get “my feedback”, effectively, via ChatGPT. It lets them test their thinking against my context and working style before coming to me. It does not make decisions or speak for me; it helps our conversations start from a stronger place.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI - The Atlantic
items.summary: People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your childrenor creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and [...] Look, I just want to say that if NVIDIA CEO and reported spy-plot target Jensen Huang did get help from AI to write an apology email to his family and company about his affair (he’s said he uses AI to help write all of his first drafts), this might be the one use of AI that makes sense to me.

items.title: Chapman Advances Healthcare AI Research and Training | Chapman Newsroom
items.summary:
“Part of embracing this technology is recognizing that we can’t send graduates into the world without knowing how to use these tools,” said Jennifer Totonchy, Ph.D., associate dean of research and graduate programs. “Ensuring our students are comfortable with AI is part of how we prepare them for future careers and stay true to our mission.” 

WHEN AI FALLS SHORT [...] Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] “We are also already seeing AI positively impact the quality of patient care in our pharmaceutical rotations, so having AI integrated into our curriculum is eye opening,” Wu said. “I don’t know many other schools that offer this kind of opportunity.”

items.title: Việt Nam - Nhật Bản hoàn tất chuyển giao công nghệ tế bào trị ung thư
items.summary:
Công nghệ tế bào gốc trung mô (MSC) hiện được nghiên cứu, phát triển trong nhiều hướng ứng dụng liên quan đến bệnh lý tim mạch, thần kinh (đột quỵ, sa sút trí tuệ), tiểu đường, bệnh phổi tắc nghẽn mạn tính (COPD), trẻ hóa da… Giải pháp tế bào miễn dịch tự nhiên (NK) mở ra cơ hội ứng dụng mới trong miễn dịch trị liệu, có thể được phối hợp với các phương pháp điều trị ung thư đa mô thức khác, như phẫu thuật, hóa trị, xạ trị và điều trị đích. [...] Hai bên lựa chọn chuyển giao các công nghệ tế bào thế hệ mới, được Tập đoàn Y tế Grandsoul, Nhật Bản nghiên cứu, phát triển và ứng dụng. Bộ Y tế, Lao động và Phúc lợi Nhật Bản (MHLW) đã phê duyệt, cấp phép ứng dụng chính thức nhiều năm tại nước này. Trọng tm gồm hai nhóm: công nghệ phn lập, nuôi cấy, biệt hóa chọn lọc tế bào gốc trung mô có nguồn gốc từ mô mỡ (Mesenchymal Stem Cells - MSC) và công nghệ phn lập nuôi cấy, biệt hóa chọn lọc tế bào miễn dịch tự nhiên NK (Natural Killer cells) điều [...] ### Từ tiếp nhận công nghệ đến năng lực tự chủ tại Việt Nam

Ông Ngô Chí Dũng, Chủ tịch HĐQT Hệ thống Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tm Anh, cho biết việc hoàn tất chuyển giao công nghệ tế bào gốc và tế bào miễn dịch từ Nhật Bản là dấu mốc quan trọng không chỉ trong hợp tác y tế hai nước, mà còn là kết nối công nghệ, thiết lập mạng lưới chuyên gia vì mục tiêu chung là chăm sóc sức khỏe cho người dn.

items.summary:

Hoàn thiện hành lang pháp lý, thúc đẩy công nghệ sinh học trong nông nghiệp

Theo TS Nguyễn Văn Long, Vụ trưởng Vụ Khoa học và Công nghệ (Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường), trong bối cảnh nông nghiệp phải đối mặt với biến đổi khí hậu, dịch bệnh và yêu cầu phát triển bền vững, việc nghiên cứu, làm chủ và ứng dụng các công nghệ tiên tiến càng trở nên cấp thiết. [...] Tổng diện tích canh tác lũy kế trong gần ba thập kỷ đạt khoảng 3,75 tỷ ha trên toàn cầu, cho thấy quy mô ứng dụng ngày càng mở rộng và sự chấp nhận ngày càng rộng rãi đối với công nghệ này trên thế giới. Đáng chú ý, việc ứng dụng cy trồng biến đổi gen không còn chỉ tập trung tại các quốc gia phát triển. Các nước đang phát triển, đặc biệt tại Mỹ Latinh, chu Á và chu Phi ngày càng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc mở rộng ứng dụng công nghệ này. [...] Đy là những kết quả bước đầu cho thấy khả năng tiếp nhận và ứng dụng công nghệ sinh học trong sản xuất nông nghiệp. Tuy nhiên, trước yêu cầu đổi mới mô hình tăng trưởng, vấn đề đặt ra không chỉ là mở rộng diện tích ứng dụng mà còn phải nng cao năng lực nghiên cứu, chủ động công nghệ và phát triển các sản phẩm có giá trị gia tăng cao.

items.summary:
THE CEO OF JAPAN'S SOFTBANK JUST ADMITTED OPENAI'S GPT-6 ASTRA FOUND 35,000 NEW SECURITY HOLES IN HIS SYSTEMS. HIS WORDS: "HONESTLY, WE'RE COMPLETELY EXHAUSTED."

June 16: emergency press conference. About 700 SoftBank systems scanned, 10,500 holes found. 3 months of patching followed.

Then: a new scan with "GPT-6 Astra", OpenAI's newest model then. 35,000 NEW holes.

Oct 7: hackers hit its cloud arm through open-source code it had never scanned. 7 minutes from alarm to damage.

Now: attackers probe its systems 600 to 700 million times a month. About double last year.

Yesterday: the CEO said each new AI model finds holes no one knew about. "We can't handle it with human hands alone."

SoftBank's new rule: if anything looks wrong, cut the line, even if service goes down. Cut first. Fix later.

None of this is a forecast. It already happened.

4 days ago, OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a security version of GPT-6 Astra, and raised its cyber risk rating from High to CRITICAL. It built working attacks for 948 Linux kernel holes.

Last week in France, hackers stole about €100 million from the bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa. In South Korea, crypto exchange GOPAX froze withdrawals and trading after a hacking threat.

At least 33 countries now tell people to stockpile at home:
🇬🇧 UK: 3 days of food and water, a power bank, cash, an FM radio
🇪🇺 EU: at least 72 hours
🇸🇪 Sweden, 🇳🇴 Norway: a full week
🇩🇪 Germany: up to 10 days
🇫🇷 🇫🇮 🇱🇹 🇱🇻 🇳🇱 🇨🇿: at least 72 hours
🇯🇵 Japan: food and water

Why FM? It works even in a blackout or a cyberattack, when phones and internet die. Britain's emergency advice: stay home, turn on an FM radio.

Britain's cyber chief Richard Horne (NCSC): "When food isn't on the shelves, when lights aren't on, businesses have gone under."

This is the AI cyberattack era. Better safe than sorry.

Follow me now. The day your bank app goes dark is a bad day to start catching up.

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] The protection of public health requires similar guidance and oversight. AI can strengthen biosurveillance by finding signals across disparate data, model and predict outbreaks, and help allocate scarce resources. We must build governance into our health system’s infrastructure that includes testing standards and protocols, continuous monitoring, ethics oversight, user education, and clear lines of accountability. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI

Leaders have to use the technology themselves: experiment, push the boundaries and learn what works. When people see that AI matters to you, it sets the tone and encourages others to engage with it.

We did not mandate usage targets. Instead, we made the technology relevant. Our business transformation team demonstrated workflows tailored to different functions, while videos, showcases, challenges and an early AI bounty surfaced ideas from across the firm. [...] The real value we’ve seen from AI so far hasn’t been about reducing cost or needing fewer people, but freeing our people to focus on the more human side of their work, meeting with clients, coaching their teams and mentoring the future leaders of our industry.

> _“It’s been about…freeing them up to then do the more human side of their work.”_

—Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer, Gilbert + Tobin [...] My team is now able to use it to get “my feedback”, effectively, via ChatGPT. It lets them test their thinking against my context and working style before coming to me. It does not make decisions or speak for me; it helps our conversations start from a stronger place.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI - The Atlantic
items.summary: People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your childrenor creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and [...] Look, I just want to say that if NVIDIA CEO and reported spy-plot target Jensen Huang did get help from AI to write an apology email to his family and company about his affair (he’s said he uses AI to help write all of his first drafts), this might be the one use of AI that makes sense to me.

items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak" - Ars Technica
items.summary: DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. [...] Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. [...] Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

OpenAI grew revenue by roughly 50% to $10 billion from the second to the third quarter, but continued to report heavy operating losses, showing mixed results in its effort to catch up with industry leader Anthropic. [...] The company shared its latest results with investors on Tuesday, just as Anthropic was preparing to mount its much-anticipated IPO next week. The maker of Claude recently disclosed that its revenue rose to $17 billion in the third quarter while reporting a smaller operating loss of $567 million during that period.

items.title: OpenAI Third-Quarter Revenue Soars Nearly 50% to $10 Billion - Bloomberg
items.summary:
# OpenAI Third-Quarter Revenue Soars Nearly 50% to $10 Billion

OpenAI’s quarterly revenue hit $10 billion for the first time in the three months ending in September, according to a person familiar with the matter, driven by strong demand for its latest artificial intelligence software. [...] The ChatGPT maker’s revenue increased nearly 50% from the prior quarter and nearly threefold from the same period a year earlier, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity as the information is not public. The financial details were shared with investors during a call on Tuesday.

items.title: OpenAI Acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder | TechCrunch
items.summary:
OpenAI did not announce this acquisition, nor confirm it to TechCrunch, when asked. Nor has it announced new travel-specific products or plans. It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners.

Travel is one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with. And, back in July, 2025, when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT agent, it mentioned travel as one of its potential uses. [...] OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson. Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel. [...] So we’ll have to wait and see what OpenAI has in store now, with his joining the company. OpenAI has not yet responded to a request for comment.
